slides.title: Robot Arm Architecture
slides.text:
Robot Arm Architecture

A robot arm is a programmable
mechanical manipulator designed to
perform tasks such as:
    –  pick-and-place,
    –  welding,
    –  painting,
    –  assembly,
    –  surgical procedures and                    SCORBOT                   Hand Arm System                                                                                German Aerospace Center (DLR)
    –  prosthetic arm
➢Machine learning (ML) for a robot arm involves
   programming the system to optimize a performance
    criterion through experience or data, rather than
    relying on fixed, hand-coded rules.


                                                                                                           4

visualInspection.notes: SCORBOT industrial articulated manipulator and DLR Hand Arm System photographs viewed. Six application bullets and ML through data/experience rather than fixed rules; photograph does not establish exact DOF.

Robot Arm Architecture

 End-Effector is the tool attached at the final joint of robot
arm.
 •   It is the interface between the robot and the physical
    world.

Type                 Measured Variables

Parallel gripper       measures contact force at each fingertip

Three-finger adaptive  multiple contact points, tactile arrays

Vacuum suction cup   suction pressure sensor

Welding torch         Current and voltage feed rate

Surgical instrument    sub-millimetre force sensing, tremor
                           filtering

Parallel fingertip force, adaptive tactile contacts, suction pressure, welding current/voltage/feed rate, surgical sensing/tremor. The exact phrase sub-millimetre force sensing mixes a length unit with force; tremor filtering is processing, not a directly measured variable.

slides.title: Fault Detection: Robotic Arm Motor
slides.text:
Fault Detection: Robotic Arm Motor

Problem Statement: Robot arm has a brushless DC motor at each joint with three
sensors sampled at 1kHz. The sensor readings are classified into two states:
normal operation and overload fault

Data Architecture: Historical fault records provide labelled examples of two
operating states.
    ➢Input Features: Current(A), Velocity(RPM), and Temperature(℃)
    ➢Target Outputs: normal operation and overload fault

Algorithm: Support Vector Machines (SVM)

Motivation: SVM allow for complex decision boundaries,
even if the data has only a few features.



                                                                                                           9

visualInspection.notes: Fault problem states BLDC motors, three sensors sampled1kHz, input current(A), speed(RPM), temperature(°C), binary normal/overload labels and supervised SVM. Sampling rate is not proven inference throughput or temporal structure of later independent synthetic draws.

slides.title: What is SVM?
slides.text:
What is SVM?

Support Vector Machines (SVMs), are a powerful class of supervised learning
 algorithms used for both
     –  classification (Support Vector Classification, or SVC) and                            Decision
                                                                             Boundary     –  regression (Support Vector Regression, or SVR).
➢We will use Support Vector Classification (SVC)


                                                  Margin➢The primary goal of an SVM is to find the optimal
   separating hyperplane, the decision boundary that
   separates classes while maximizing the margin.
➢The Goal of the SVM is to maximize this distance to provide a
   "breathing space" that helps the model generalize better to
   new data.

                                                                                                          10

visualInspection.notes: SVC/SVR bullets and sklearn.svm SVC import viewed; central solid decision boundary between blue circles and red triangles, parallel dashed margins. SVM separates in chosen feature space; nonlinear input boundaries possible with kernel.

slides.title: Inverse Kinematic: 2R Planar Robotic Arm
slides.text:
Inverse Kinematic: 2R Planar Robotic Arm

Problem Statement: Predicting joint angles for a 2-Degree-of-Freedom (2R)
planar robotic arm using Machine Learning.
System Parameters: Link Length 𝐿1 = 𝐿2 = 1𝑚

Algorithm: Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) Regression.
Data Architecture:
   ➢Input Features: Desired end-effector coordinates (𝑥, 𝑦).
    ➢Target Outputs: Corresponding joint angles  𝜃1, 𝜃2  .

Motivation:
•  Overcoming limitations of analytical/numerical
    (e.g., computational cost, multiple solution) IK solvers.



                                                                                                           17

visualInspection.notes: Planar2R problem with L1=L2=1m, input(x,y), output(theta1,theta2), MLP regression. Motivation does not prove learned IK eliminates branches or is faster/more accurate than analytic2R solution.

slides.title: What is MLP Regression?
slides.text:
What is MLP Regression?


In scikit-learn, MLP Regression is the estimator class used to
implement Multilayer Perceptron (MLPs) for regression tasks.
•  MLPs, Multilayer perceptron are also known as (vanilla) feed-
   forward neural networks, or sometimes just neural
   networks.
•  The architecture of an MLP for regression consists of an input
    layer, one or more hidden layers, and an output layer.
•   Multilayer perceptron is for classification and regression,
   serve as a starting point for more involved deep learning
   methods.




                                                                                                          18

visualInspection.notes: Actual sklearn.neural_network MLPRegressor import. Generic drawing has four input nodes x[0..3], three hidden h[0..2], one output; not the later2in/2out IK architecture. mglearn plot_single_hidden_layer_graph display snippet presumes mglearn/display setup not shown.

slides.title: Inverse Kinematic: 2R Planar Robotic Arm
slides.text:
Inverse Kinematic: 2R Planar Robotic Arm

➢Dataset:(𝑋, 𝑦) = ( 𝑥, 𝑦, 𝜃1, 𝜃2 )
    For creating dataset (X,y) we will use Forward kinematic
   equation
   𝑥 = 𝐿1 ∗𝑛𝑝. cos(𝜃1) + 𝐿2 ∗𝑛𝑝. cos(𝜃1 + 𝜃2)
   𝑦 = 𝐿1 ∗𝑛𝑝. sin 𝜃1 + 𝐿2 ∗𝑛𝑝. sin(𝜃1 + 𝜃2)
➢In IK we will add constrain as multiple solution
   possible for elbow-up (𝜃2 = −𝜋 𝑡𝑜 0 rad) and
  elbow-down (𝜃2 = 0 𝑡𝑜 𝜋 rad)
➢Joint angle 𝜃1, 𝜃2 are constrained
    𝜃1 = −180° 𝑡𝑜 +180°= −𝜋 𝑡𝑜 𝜋 rad
    𝜃2 = 0 𝑡𝑜+180°= 0 𝑡𝑜 𝜋 rad        elbow-down



                                                                                                          20

visualInspection.notes: Both FK equations clearly include cos(theta1+theta2)/sin(theta1+theta2). X=[x,y], targets=[theta1,theta2]. Diagram two elbow configurations reaching same P; source calls theta2 positive elbow-down and negative elbow-up. theta1[-pi,pi],theta2[0,pi] branch used. Branch selection does not remove theta1 wrap seam or center singularity.
